_meta.title: Drift-Pack Library
_meta.purpose: Ordered sound-change rulesets that age or shift a language. Selected per derivation (Gap 1 fix). Replaces the single hard-coded SOUND_CHANGE_RULES stub in engine.ts.
_meta.how_they_fit: deriveCulture / driftWord take one or more packs instead of a bare intensity. Rules apply in listed ORDER as a single pass (order enables feeding chains, e.g. p>b then b>v turns intervocalic p into v). Intensity (dialect/sister/distant) becomes a probability multiplier on whether each rule fires, so 'how far along the chain' stays tunable.
_meta.the_ease_law_resolved: The framework says 'drift always becomes easier.' Fortition (hardening) isn't strictly easier, so each pack carries a 'direction': 'erosion' packs (softening, compression) obey the ease law and are the safe default; 'shift' packs (vowel-shift, hardening) are systematic, consistent remaps that need not ease articulation. The Step 6 name gate runs on all output regardless, so shift packs cannot produce unreadable names.

rule_shape.from: grapheme(s) to match (may be multi-char: geminates 'tt', digraphs 'dh', diphthongs 'ae')

when_vocabulary.unstressed: in an unstressed syllable; engine approximates as non-initial-syllable. Engine MUST guard the result through the joinery/gate check, since vowel deletion here can create clusters.

_meta.capitalization_and_dash: Rules operate on the lowercased core. The engine preserves a leading capital (start-slot marker) and a leading '-' (end-slot marker) around the transformation, exactly as the current driftWord already does.
_meta.validation: drift_validator.py enforces this schema, family/direction consistency, the ease heuristic on erosion packs, the 26-letter constraint on outputs, inverse-pair and duplicate detection, and prints a before/after demo per pack. A FAIL blocks the build.

effect_families.softening: erosion — consonants weaken toward voiced stops, fricatives, or h
effect_families.compression: erosion — vowels reduce and delete; length falls
effect_families.hardening: shift — consonants fortify; final obstruents devoice
effect_families.reshaping: shift — adapts a foreign form to a borrower's simpler phonology (contact loanwords)

romance_softening.plainDescription: Hard stops soften and voice between vowels, then spirantise; doubles simplify.
romance_softening.why: The Western Romance path (Latin to Spanish/Italian): vita-like forms wear toward vida-like ones. Names come out fluid and worn.

rules.gloss: voiceless stop p voices between vowels
voiceless stop t voices between vowels
voiceless stop k/c voices between vowels
voiceless stop k voices between vowels
voiced stop b spirantises (feeds from p>b)
voiced stop d spirantises to a soft th (feeds from t>d)
voiced stop g spirantises (feeds from c/k>g)

celtic_lenition.plainDescription: Intervocalic consonants weaken toward fricatives and h; m goes to v, s goes to h.
celtic_lenition.why: The Celtic lenition pattern: consonants soften between vowels in distinctive ways (s>h, m>v) that give a different flavour from the Romance path.

rules.gloss: k/c weakens to a back fricative
k weakens to a back fricative
d spirantises to a soft th

vowel_melting.plainDescription: Adjacent vowels merge; doubled vowels collapse.
vowel_melting.why: The path toward French-like smoothing, where vowel clusters melt into single sounds and endings blur.

syllable_erosion.plainDescription: Intervocalic h drops, final unstressed vowels fall away, and resulting doubles simplify.
syllable_erosion.why: The literal 'Ban-hok becomes Bannock' path (rassaku Part III): speakers wear names down toward what is easiest to say. The clearest demonstration of the ease law.

vowel_shift.plainDescription: A push chain: back vowels raise and the long high front vowel diphthongises. Consonants untouched.
vowel_shift.why: The Great-Vowel-Shift feel. Ordered as a push chain (o>u fires before a>o) so the vowels rotate without merging into each other.

rules.gloss: mid back vowel raises (fires first to clear the slot)
low vowel raises into the vacated slot

germanic_hardening.plainDescription: A Grimm-style consonant shift plus final-obstruent devoicing.
germanic_hardening.why: The Germanic path: p/t/k become fricatives while b/d/g harden into p/t/k. Ordered so the two waves stay distinct in a single pass.

rules.gloss: voiceless stop spirantises (wave 1, fires before b>p)
voiced stop hardens into the vacated p slot (wave 2)
tidy: a stop spirantising beside an existing th leaves th, not thh

prestige_exonym.plainDescription: Adapts a foreign name to a borrower who lacks its harder sounds: fricatives plainen, exotic letters simplify, glottal marks drop.
prestige_exonym.why: The Confucius mechanic. A donor form is worn to the borrower's simpler phonology as it crosses the contact edge, which is also a readability win. Used by contact edges, not descent chains.

rules.gloss: borrower lacks the soft-th, hears a plain d
borrower lacks the back fricative, hears a plain g
borrower reads x as a plain k
borrower ignores the glottal mark it cannot say
